KNOWN_PREFILLS.measured: Two separate things measured, and the second is a failure. FIRST, the eight field writes are correct and the map does not disagree with the finalizer. production-field-map declares exactly four explicitMappings per petition - PetitionerName1 to participant.full_legal_name, PetAdd1 to street_address, PetAdd2 to city_state_zip, PetPhoneNum to phone - and the delivered bytes carry exactly four text-bearing flattened appearances per petition and no others, read out of every /FlatWidget XObject on all four pages of each: 'Jordan Avery Reyes', '42 Maple Street, Apartment 3', 'Charleston, WV 25301', '304-555-0142'. The map-honest-writes-not defect class is absent and its two known limbs are clean: item d, 'Petitioner's current name, previous names, and all aliases', carries no ink on either petition in either fixture, and item e, 'All of petitioner's addresses from the date of offense to current', likewise. Both are declared REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING and disclosed. The verification page carries no ink at all. SECOND, AND THIS IS THE FAILURE, the composed supplemental pleading - a document the packet itself says on its face is filed with the petition, captioned IN THE CIRCUIT COURT OF ____ COUNTY, WEST VIRGINIA - recites its own controlling records' words, with the internal framing printed. Read off delivered pages 9 and 10: item 2 and item 3 each print the line 'From the packet record, in its own words:' followed by a verbatim participant instruction - 'Obtain Documentation of compliance ... Ask the programme provider for written documentation of your compliance, covering the dates you were in the programme, and ask them to confirm in writing that the programme is approved by the Secretary of the Department of Health' and 'Obtain Certificate of graduation ... Ask the course provider for your certificate of graduation'; item 4 prints 'Eligibility clock. The route record for this petition states it as follows:' and quotes it; the signature block prints 'Signature requirement, from the route record: "The petitioner signs the petition and the supplemental pleading, swears the verification before a notary public or other official ..."'; item 1 prints '(write TREATMENT, JOB READINESS, or BOTH - whichever describes what you are relying on. Only you know which)'; item 5 prints '(list what you are actually attaching, from the checklist in this packet)'; and the page closes 'This pleading was prepared from the petitioner's own details and from the packet record.' The 'Obtain ...' paragraphs are word-for-word the same strings the RECORDS CHECKLIST prints on delivered page 11, so the guide's own text is on the filing. This is the internal-record-text-printed-on-a-filing class in the Captain's DEFECTS_NO_COUNTER_CAN_SEE record, whose fix is stated as: filings recite statute citations and rule text only, and the record's own words belong in the guide, labelled as internal record text. The builder's own build-findings shows it repaired only the machine-vocabulary instance of this - the serialized tuple 'elapsed_eligibility_clock - 90 days - disposition_date - ...' that its first render printed - by switching to a recordProse quoter that takes the record's prose sentence. That half is genuinely fixed: I scanned the whole 14-page delivered text for snake_case, template braces, null, undefined, NaN, schemaVersion, routeKey, familyId and the obligation: prefix and found zero hits, and the elapsed_eligibility_clock string appears nowhere. But the framing that names the internal record on the face of a filing was not removed, and it is still a court filing that tells a circuit judge what 'the route record for this petition' and 'the packet record' say, and that instructs the petitioner to go and ask a provider for documents.

SELF_HELP_STOP.measured: This is the second failure and it is the more serious of the two. The committed legal-design-track-registry entry for wv_acc_treatment_job_readiness carries TEN selfHelpStopConditions. I checked each one against participant-instructions.md and against the full extracted text of all 14 delivered pages, normalised for dashes, quotes and the section sign. NINE of the ten appear in neither: 'Any felony conviction, which is a referral trigger on this route as on wv_conv_nonviolent_felony'; 'Any doubt whether the treatment or recovery programme is approved by the Secretary of the Department of Health, or the job readiness course by the West Virginia Department of Education'; 'Any violence, domestic violence, household member, strangulation, sex, child victim, deadly weapon, dwelling burglary or DUI issue'; 'Any CDL or commercial motor vehicle issue'; 'Any pending charge'; 'Any protection, no-contact, restitution or restraining order'; 'Any identified victim who may oppose, and any notice of opposition actually filed'; 'Any prior expungement, which likely exhausts the once-per-lifetime rule that this section shares with section 61-11-26'; and 'Firearm rights, immigration, professional licensing, law enforcement or corrections employment, or federal, tribal, military or out-of-state records questions'. The only one present is 'The court sets the matter for hearing', and it is present only incidentally, inside the single postGenerationHandoffs sentence. There is no stop section of any kind: the guide's twelve headings contain nothing like 'when to stop and get help', and the word 'lawyer' occurs once in the guide and once in the whole delivered packet, in the IF IT IS OPPOSED line on page 14. The first stop condition is the one that matters most here, because this packet ships SCA-C907, the FELONY petition, as one of its two conditional primary filings and tells the participant on page 13 to file it 'where the conviction to be expunged is a nonviolent felony' - while the family's own registry says any felony conviction is a referral trigger on this route. A participant with a felony is handed the felony petition and is never told that their own route record says that is the point to get a lawyer. Two further registry entries bear on the same gap and are also absent from every delivered page and from the guide: the scopeRestriction 'One open question first: whether a single misdemeanor qualifies under this section at all ... Do not ship the 90-day single-misdemeanor row until that is confirmed', and the releaseBlocker on how the section 61-11-26a(a)(1) ninety-day clock interacts with the section 61-11-26(b)(1) one-year clock. Both are undisclosed while delivered page 10 and the guide's own opening both state the clock as settled: 'ninety days of programme compliance OR completion of an approved job readiness adult training course ... the accelerated clock replaces the Sec. 61-11-26(b)(1) one-year wait for a single misdemeanour'. That is the exact row the scope restriction says not to ship.

FILING_DESTINATION.measured: Stated, sourced and consistent across the three channels. The track registry venue is 'The circuit court or circuit courts in which the conviction or convictions occurred, section 61-11-26a(a)' and its destination is 'Clerk of the circuit court of the county of conviction'. Delivered page 13 prints 'WHERE IT GOES' with that venue sentence quoted, and the FILING paragraph gives the fuller rule including which petition goes with what. The guide says the same at its 'Where it goes and what it costs' heading. Both petitions' captions are 'IN THE CIRCUIT COURT OF ____ COUNTY, WEST VIRGINIA' with the county blank left to the participant and declared REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING. Nothing overstates a filing channel: no eFiling claim, no clerk practice and no deadline is asserted, and the build-findings record correctly that the route-obligation census holds nothing for filingMethod, filingDeadline or postFilingInstructions, so none is stated.

SERVICE.measured: Recipients and method are both answered and the one real tension is disclosed rather than papered over. The registry rule is 'The petitioner serves the five section 61-11-26(e) recipients. The prosecuting attorney serves identified victims', and both the guide and delivered page 13 print it verbatim. The forms themselves print more than five: I counted the printed numbered items on the delivered certificate pages - eight on SCA-C906 and seven on SCA-C907 - and the packet resolves the mismatch the right way, by telling the participant on page 13 that 'the certificate of service page of whichever petition you file lists the recipients the form itself names, and you write each address'. The builder's read-the-paper finding here is correct and I verified it independently from the source bytes: SCA-C907 has no 'Chief Law Enforcement Officer of any other Law Enforcement Agency' item at all, and its widgets ChiefLEO1 (rect y 402.9-420.2) and ChiefLEO2 (y 380.8-398.1) sit between the printed item 4 'The Superintendent or Warden of any Institution in which Petitioner was confined' at y 448/434 and item 5 at y 378 - so on that form those two widgets are the Superintendent-or-Warden answer lines, not a police line. Nothing is written into any of them on either petition, and the guide labels each line from the printed item rather than the field name, so the mislabelling could not reach a participant. Timing is handled: the packet writes nothing on the certificate, not even the petitioner's own name, and says in terms that the page is completed and signed on the day service actually happens.

Field level: production-field-map declares 123 requiredBeforeFiling blanks and all 123 are disclosed in participant-instructions.md by exact string containment on both the disclosureLabel and the full why text, 123 of 123, checked here. Record level: the committed packet-set manifest carries 19 participantActionRequired entries and 17 requiredBeforeFiling strings, including four obtain_document items. All four obtain_document items appear verbatim in the guide under 'The documents you must have before you file' AND on delivered page 11, so the Massachusetts sibling's failure - a committed obtain_document item the guide never states - is not present here. The residual, recorded rather than scored: reports/blanks-left-for-the-participant.json asserts everyRequiredBeforeFilingItemIsDisclosed true with disclosedIn naming participant-instructions.md, over an array that holds only the 123 form blanks, and nine of the manifest's own record-level items are in fact absent from that file - the four confirm_answer items and five complete_field items (rehabilitation statement, the nonviolent-felony characterisation, the signature and notarial block, the certificate-of-service completion, and the circuit court case number). They are not undisclosed: every one of the nine is printed on delivered page 12 under 'Then check your own answers against those documents' and 'And complete these by hand before filing'. So the disclosure reaches the participant and the assertion's stated scope is simply narrower than what it claims.

ROUTE_OPTIONS.measured: MEASURED against the printed paragraphs, which is the only evidence that counts on these two forms. Part (c) of each petition prints four eligibility branches. Read off the delivered pages: on SCA-C906 branches 1 and 2 recite section 61-11-26 alone (one year for a single misdemeanour, two years for multiple) and branches 3 and 4 recite the section 61-11-26a(1)/(2) requirements; on SCA-C907 branches 1 and 2 recite section 61-11-26 alone (five years) and branches 3 and 4 recite section 61-11-26a(a)(1)/(a)(2). So the two-accelerated-two-ordinary split the build asserts is what the paper actually prints. The route rules out the two ordinary branches, which are declared NOT_APPLICABLE_ON_THIS_ROUTE with the reason, and leaves the two accelerated ones to the participant on a single-versus-multiple basis, declared REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING. All four boxes are delivered unticked, confirmed from the bytes. I verified the builder's read-the-paper finding independently: SCA-C906's four Part (c) boxes really are named SingleFelonyCB, MultipleFelonyCB, SingleSatisfiedCB and MultilpleSatisfiedCB with date blanks SingleFelonyCompletionDate, MultipleFelonyCompletionDate, SingleFelonySatisfiesDate and MulitipleFelonlySatisfiesDate - felony names throughout - on a form whose printed caption is PETITION FOR EXPUNGEMENT OF MISDEMEANOR VIOLATIONS AND TRAFFIC CITATIONS, read from the pinned binary's own AcroForm. theMatrixCheckThisLaneWasAskedFor.question: Does every flattened checkbox XObject in the delivered bytes carry a /Matrix that cancels its placement translate, and do the boxes actually land in the left margin where the paper prints them?
theMatrixCheckThisLaneWasAskedFor.howMeasured: Parsed every page content stream of canonical.pdf, boundary.pdf and all four per-petition fixtures with pikepdf, tracked the CTM through q/Q/cm, and for every /FlatWidget Do read that XObject's /BBox and /Matrix out of its dictionary. Then rendered the pages with pdftoppm at 130 dpi and looked at them.
theMatrixCheckThisLaneWasAskedFor.result: CONFIRMED, on the delivered bytes and on the rendered page.
theMatrixCheckThisLaneWasAskedFor.measurement: canonical.pdf carries 143 flattened widget appearances, of which 26 are the checkbox appearances (13 per petition, drawn as vector rectangles with no BT). Every one of the 26 has a page-coordinate /BBox and a /Matrix of exactly [1 0 0 1 -bbox.x -bbox.y], and is placed by a cm whose translation equals that same bbox origin. Worked example, SingleFelonyCB on SCA-C906 page 1: BBox [91.68 324.91 103.2 336.43], /Matrix [1 0 0 1 -91.68 -324.91], placement '1 0 0 1 91.68 324.91 cm'. The form matrix cancels the translate, so the composed transform puts the stream's own absolute coordinates back where they belong, and the ink lands at (91.7, 324.9)-(103.2, 336.4) - the widget's own rectangle. Zero problems across all six fixtures: 26 of 26 cancel on canonical.pdf and on boundary.pdf, 13 of 13 on each per-petition fixture, and no appearance is placed anywhere but at its own bbox origin. The 117 remaining flattened appearances carry origin-based BBoxes with an identity matrix, which is the generated-appearance shape and needs no cancellation.
theMatrixCheckThisLaneWasAskedFor.andItLooksRight: Rendered page 1 of SCA-C906 and of SCA-C907. On both, the four Part (c) boxes stand in the left margin, one beside each of the four printed eligibility paragraphs, and there is no stray square beside 'IN RE: Expungement of Record of:', none on the caption rule, none inside the fourth CHARGE line and none inside the word 'traffic'. Page 2 of each carries its four victim-order Yes/No boxes each immediately left of its own label, page 3 its two, and page 4 the three service-method boxes each beside First Class Mail, Hand Delivery and Certified Mail. Twenty-six boxes, twenty-six correct positions.
theMatrixCheckThisLaneWasAskedFor.whyThisNeededTwoMethods: The builder's own build-findings records that its first byte proof could not see this class either, because matching the placement operator's translation against the widget rectangle answers whether an appearance was PLACED at a widget, not whether its ink FALLS INSIDE one. The reading with teeth is the one above - composing /BBox through /Matrix and the placement - and it is confirmed by rendering.

SELF_HELP_STOP.measured: FAIL. The committed track registry names four selfHelpStopConditions for ma-seal-court. Two reach the participant, both only as description rather than as a stop: 'The prosecutor opposes' and 'A hearing is set and the participant must attend' appear inside the guide's 'What happens after you file', where the operative sentence is the record's own internal handoff instruction quoted at the reader - 'Hand off when a hearing is actually set or the prosecutor opposes' - which tells a self-represented filer nothing about what to do. Two reach nobody: 'The case is nearly old enough for the ministerial route, where waiting may be better advice' and 'The disposition may be one of the three automatic-sealing dispositions rather than a dismissal' appear in neither participant-instructions.md nor any delivered page, checked by normalised containment and then by grepping for 'ministerial', 'automatic' and '100A', all of which return nothing. Those two are the ones that matter most to a participant, because each says the petition may be unnecessary: one that the record may seal itself, the other that waiting gets a simpler route. And there is no stop-and-get-help section of any kind - the word 'lawyer' occurs ZERO times in the guide, and the only boundary statement is 'What this packet is not', which says the packet is not legal advice but never says where automated help ends. This is the standard this lane's peers applied hours ago: VF03 failed ia-12347-set on SELF_HELP_STOP because one of two registry conditions reached nobody and no stop section existed, and VF05 and VF04 failed the Illinois families on the same reading.

FILING_DESTINATION.measured: Answered better than most. The registry venue is quoted whole and then explained in the participant's own terms, and the unusual limb is called out: a District Court case goes back to the clerk's office where the case started, while a Boston Municipal Court case goes to the BMC division where the participant LIVES, or if they no longer live in BMC territory to the division the most recent eligible record is from. The guide puts that section before the COURT DIVISION/COUNTY blank and tells the participant to work the division out from the rule before writing it, which is the right order. 'Use a separate form for each case' is stated twice, once quoted from the form's own face. The destination the registry names, the clerk's office of the court identified by the venue rule, is what the guide names.

SERVICE.measured: The right answer here is that the participant serves nobody, and the packet says so and says why. The registry records service as 'Per the court's practice on the form' and notice as the Clerk-Magistrate's act, and the delivered page 2 prints the court's own block: the Clerk-Magistrate must give notice of the hearing to the Probation Service and the appropriate prosecutor's office, who should notify any victims, and must post a copy of the petition on a public bulletin board until the hearing. The guide quotes that block verbatim and then states in terms that the route record records no service recipient, method or timing for this route and that what the form prints is that the Clerk-Magistrate gives the notices, not the participant, so nothing further is stated. It also surfaces the public-posting consequence in plain words before filing, which is the thing a participant would least expect. No service act, deadline or recipient is invented.

REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.measured: FAIL, and it is the same defect, on the same evidence, that failed the sibling ma-expunge-k-set earlier today. TWO COMMITTED RECORDS make obtaining a CORI a required-before-filing act. data/record-clearing/legal-design-packet-set-manifests.json, packetSet ma-seal-court-set, participantActionRequired[0]: kind obtain_document, requirement required, requiredBeforeFiling true, obtainedFrom 'Massachusetts Department of Criminal Justice Information Services', description 'Obtain Your own CORI from the Department of Criminal Justice Information Services. Request your personal CORI from DCJIS. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.' The same string is the first entry of that packetSet's requiredBeforeFiling array. data/record-clearing/legal-design-track-registry.json, track ma-seal-court, packetSet.participantActionRequired[0] carries the identical item, and [1] is the paired confirm_answer, 'Check your answer to "What is the docket number?" against Your own CORI ... and correct the packet if they disagree', also requiredBeforeFiling true. WHAT THE DELIVERED GUIDE SAYS: I read participant-instructions.md end to end and grepped it. CORI appears three times and all three are as an optional alternative source to copy FROM, never as a document to obtain - line 36 'The platform has never seen your court record or your CORI', line 42 'the charge as it is written on your own court papers or your CORI', line 115 'copied from your own court papers or from your CORI'. DCJIS is never named, in the guide or on any delivered page. The guide has a 'What to bring with it' section and it names one attachment, the disposition record, not the CORI. Its nine-step 'What you must do, in order' list has no obtain step and no cross-check step. A participant who follows that list holding their court papers never obtains a CORI and never performs the confirm_answer check, because neither is stated. WHY IT READS CLEAN: reports/blanks-left-for-the-participant.json asserts everyRequiredBeforeFilingItemIsDisclosed true with disclosedIn naming participant-instructions.md, over an array of 127 entries which its own requiredBeforeFilingByGroup block shows are all FORM BLANKS - captionAndIdentity 3, courtDepartmentBoxes 4, chargeTableCells 111, nineNarrativeAnswers 9. The controlling records' participant-action strings are outside that array's scope, so the assertion is true of a narrower set than its name claims. The field-level channel itself is sound and I verified it separately: all 127 declared blanks appear in the guide by exact string containment, 127 of 127, including every one of the 111 charge cells individually.
